Title: As Fate
On-Screen Text: when an inner situation / is not made conscious, / it happens outside, / as fate. / — carl jung · aion, 1951
Caption: this is the jung line everyone shares as "until you make the unconscious conscious, it will direct your life and you will call it fate." he never wrote that sentence. this is what he actually wrote, in aion, 1951. and honestly? the real one is sharper. the pattern you refuse to look at doesn't disappear. it starts showing up as other people, other jobs, other relationships. same lesson, new outfit. look at it on purpose and it stops having to find you. ♡ - MK

Title: The Confidence of Options
On-Screen Text: detachment isn't / indifference. / it's the confidence / of options. / — the manifest
Caption: the most attractive thing you can bring to anything (a sale, a date, a negotiation) is being genuinely fine either way. not because you don't care. because your worth isn't riding on one yes. widen your options and the grip loosens on its own. chase it and it runs. ♡ - MK

Title: Making the Darkness Conscious
On-Screen Text: one does not become enlightened / by imagining figures of light, / but by making / the darkness conscious. / — carl jung · alchemical studies
Caption: the light-and-love version of healing skips the hard part. jung didn't. you don't get enlightened by imagining figures of light. you get there by making the darkness conscious. the jealousy. the old fear. the part of you that still wants to be chosen. name it and it loses the dark room it was hiding in. ♡ - MK

Title: Within Our Power
On-Screen Text: there are things / which are within our power, / and there are things / which are beyond our power. / — epictetus · enchiridion
Caption: epictetus was born enslaved and became one of the great teachers of stoicism, and this is how his handbook opens. sort everything into two piles. in your power: your effort, your words, your next move. not in your power: their reply, the timeline, the outcome. spend your energy on the first pile. detachment is just good sorting. ♡ - MK

Title: Faith in Shaking Hands

Caption: i used to wait to feel certain before i moved. certainty never came. what came was this: faith isn't the absence of fear. it's walking through the door anyway, hands shaking, heart loud. that's the whole memoir, really. ♡ - MK

Title: What Irritates Us
On-Screen Text: everything that irritates us / about others / can lead us to an understanding / of ourselves. / — carl jung · memories, dreams, reflections
Caption: one of the most useful lines jung ever wrote is tucked into his memoir. the thing that irritates you most in someone else is usually pointing at something in you. a need you've denied. a trait you were punished for. a freedom you never gave yourself. next time someone gets under your skin, ask what they're showing you. ♡ - MK

Title: Not the Fruits
On-Screen Text: you have a right / to your actions, / but never / to their fruits. / — bhagavad gita 2.47
Caption: the bhagavad gita said it two thousand years before anyone called it the law of detachment. do the work fully. give it everything. then let go of what it pays you back. the outcome was never yours to hold. the effort always was. ♡ - MK

Title: Everyone Carries a Shadow
On-Screen Text: everyone carries a shadow, / and the less it is embodied / in the individual's conscious life, / the blacker and denser it is. / — carl jung · psychology and religion, 1938
Caption: this is jung's clearest warning about the shadow. what you push down doesn't shrink. it gets denser. the anger you swallow, the ambition you call selfish, the grief you never had time for. bring them into the light and they become information. keep them in the dark and they make your decisions for you. ♡ - MK

Title: Not the Only Thing
On-Screen Text: name what happened / without letting it become / the only thing / that is true about you. / — rebecoming
Caption: what happened to you is true. it is not the only true thing. you can tell the story honestly without letting it write the rest of the book. remember it. release what it taught you to perform. then rewrite. ♡ - MK

Title: Who Looks Inside
On-Screen Text: who looks outside, dreams; / who looks inside, / awakes. / — carl jung · letter, 1916
Caption: jung wrote this in a 1916 letter to a woman about to start working with him. it still reads like a dare. we spend so much time studying other people's choices, other people's lives, other people's opinions of us. that's the dream. waking up happens when you finally turn around and look in. ♡ - MK
